title: Nvidia’s $3.5B MediaTek bet reveals its plan for tackling Big Tech’s AI chip buildout

questions.question: Will NVIDIA complete its reported $3.5 billion investment in MediaTek by January 31, 2027?
questions.why_it_matters: A $3.5 billion investment is a material use of NVIDIA’s capital. Completion would also deepen a strategic partnership intended to extend NVIDIA-compatible infrastructure into custom chips developed for AI companies and hyperscalers. The article reports the investment but does not establish that it has closed.
questions.why_not_already_covered: The existing questions cover other NVIDIA investments and financing obligations, but none tracks the reported MediaTek investment. The central outcome here is whether this specific investment is completed, not the broader AI-capex cycle, NVIDIA revenue, or custom-silicon competition.
questions.how_and_when_to_check: Check by January 31, 2027, an analyst check date at NVIDIA’s FY2027 year-end; the article states no transaction-closing date. Look for closing or transaction announcements from NVIDIA or MediaTek and relevant company filings or official disclosures. The article reports that NVIDIA is investing, not that the investment has been completed.

evidence.quote: Nvidia is investing $3.5 billion into Taiwanese chipmaker MediaTek.
evidence.what_it_shows: The article reports the investment and its stated amount, but does not say that the investment has closed or provide a closing date.

evidence.quote: As part of the deal, MediaTek will adopt Nvidia’s technology that will help it design custom chips for AI companies and hyperscalers that can be plugged directly into Nvidia-based data centers.
evidence.what_it_shows: Describes the strategic purpose of the transaction: linking MediaTek’s custom-chip work to NVIDIA-based data centers. This helps explain why completion could matter beyond the capital outlay.

evidence.quote: The deal comes as a growing number of AI companies and major cloud providers like Amazon, Google, Microsoft, OpenAI and Anthropic invest in building their own chips so they can be less reliant on Nvidia’s GPUs.
evidence.what_it_shows: Provides competitive context: customers are developing alternatives to NVIDIA GPUs, making the reported partnership’s ability to keep custom chips within NVIDIA’s infrastructure ecosystem strategically relevant.

evidence.quote: Deals like this one with MediaTek allow Nvidia to cede ground to custom silicon while still maintaining its lead as the dominant data center scaffolding.
evidence.what_it_shows: The journalist’s assessment of the partnership’s strategic rationale: NVIDIA may accommodate custom silicon while retaining a role in the surrounding data-center infrastructure.

evidence.quote: The partnership underscores the circular nature of Nvidia’s financing efforts over the past few years, which have often seen the chip giant investing in companies that flow back into its own ecosystem.
evidence.what_it_shows: Frames the investment as part of NVIDIA’s broader financing approach, in which investments may reinforce demand for or use of its ecosystem; it does not confirm the MediaTek investment’s completion.

evidence.quote: The deal will give MediaTek access to Nvidia’s NVLink Fusion ecosystem, including NVLink, the technology that lets any chips — even if they’re not Nvidia’s chips — communicate with each other quickly.
evidence.what_it_shows: Identifies the ecosystem access associated with the deal and explains how NVIDIA technology could remain relevant when customers deploy non-NVIDIA chips.

evidence.quote: Last week, Nvidia announced a similar partnership with Amazon Web Services, albeit without the direct investment.
evidence.what_it_shows: Shows that NVIDIA is pursuing a similar ecosystem partnership without an investment in another case. This is context, not evidence that the MediaTek investment has closed.

evidence.quote: AWS will deploy an additional 2 million Nvidia GPUs across its infrastructure, and also integrate NVLink Fusion.
evidence.what_it_shows: Gives an example of a related partnership involving NVIDIA GPUs and NVLink Fusion. It supports the strategic context but does not resolve the MediaTek investment’s status.

evidence.quote: With the Nvidia partnership, MediaTek can continue to build custom chips designed by cloud companies or AI labs tailored to their workloads, leveraging Nvidia’s “proven scale-up and scale-out technology stack and ecosystem” and “rack-scale architecture.”
evidence.what_it_shows: Explains the anticipated relationship between MediaTek’s custom-chip business and NVIDIA’s infrastructure. The quoted descriptions are attributed by the article to NVIDIA’s technology stack and architecture.
evidence.original_speaker: Article’s reporting; the phrases “proven scale-up and scale-out technology stack and ecosystem” and “rack-scale architecture” are quoted descriptions in the article

evidence.quote: “Basically, every cloud, every model builder is deploying our platform in some shape, form, or fashion,” Harris said. “So by MediaTek being able to offer this extension to its customers, it allows them to standardize on the rack-scale infrastructure across their AI factories… and also deploy their [custom chips] right alongside those using the same standard platform.”
evidence.what_it_shows: NVIDIA’s Harris describes the intended benefit: MediaTek customers could use custom chips alongside NVIDIA-based systems on a shared rack-scale platform. This supports the strategic importance of the partnership, not confirmation of investment closing.
evidence.original_speaker: Dion Harris, NVIDIA’s senior director of HPC and AI hyperscaler infrastructure solutions

evidence.quote: “This is really about opening up this ecosystem to the entire MediaTek customer base,” Harris continued.
evidence.what_it_shows: Harris characterizes the partnership as an effort to extend NVIDIA’s ecosystem across MediaTek’s customers.
evidence.original_speaker: Dion Harris, NVIDIA’s senior director of HPC and AI hyperscaler infrastructure solutions

evidence.quote: MediaTek hasn’t publicly shared information about its customer base as it relates to custom AI chips, but it’s clear Nvidia aims to help it boost that side of the business so long as it can come along for the ride.
evidence.what_it_shows: Notes a limitation on evidence about MediaTek’s custom-AI-chip customers and the journalist’s view of NVIDIA’s objective. It does not provide confirmation of investment completion.

evidence.quote: MediaTek has been slowly building its custom data center ASIC (application-specific integrated circuit) operations, saying in June that it expects the business to generate $2 billion in revenue in 2026, and hopes to target more of the market in the coming years.
evidence.what_it_shows: Provides a forecast from MediaTek about its custom data-center ASIC business, indicating the commercial opportunity associated with the partnership. The $2 billion is an expectation for 2026, not reported revenue or evidence that NVIDIA’s investment has closed.
evidence.original_speaker: MediaTek, as reported by the article

evidence.quote: Given MediaTek’s expertise in developing custom chips that power smartphones , smart homes, automobiles, and wireless communications, the company will also continue to collaborate with Nvidia on DGX Spark, the company’s small developer-focused desktop AI computer.
evidence.what_it_shows: Adds context on MediaTek’s existing chip-development expertise and a continuing collaboration on DGX Spark, but does not establish the investment’s completion.

evidence.quote: The companies have extended their collaboration with the RTX Spark, Nvidia’s push to put its AI tech into consumer AI PCs.
evidence.what_it_shows: Reports an extended collaboration on RTX Spark as further partnership context; it does not state that the $3.5 billion investment has closed.

evidence.quote: MediaTek and Nvidia will also continue “developing platforms for AI-powered, software-defined vehicles in the era of physical AI,” per a press release.
evidence.what_it_shows: Reports another area of ongoing collaboration, attributed to a press release, illustrating the partnership’s breadth without resolving the investment’s completion.
evidence.original_speaker: MediaTek and NVIDIA, per a press release

evidence.quote: MediaTek’s auto platforms rely on Nvidia’s RTX graphics for intelligent vehicle cockpits and work alongside Nvidia Drive AGX, the company’s in-car computing platform for autonomous driving workloads.
evidence.what_it_shows: Describes an existing technical relationship in automotive platforms, providing additional strategic context but no evidence about closing the investment.

evidence.quote: “AI is transforming every computing platform — from the world’s largest AI factories to the PC and the car,” Jensen Huang, founder and CEO of Nvidia, said in a statement. “Together, we’re building platforms that bring NVIDIA accelerated computing to new markets and give customers the freedom to create differentiated AI systems at enormous scale.”
evidence.what_it_shows: Huang states NVIDIA’s broader strategic aim of extending accelerated computing across markets and enabling differentiated systems. The statement supports the partnership rationale but does not confirm the investment’s completion.
evidence.original_speaker: Jensen Huang, NVIDIA founder and CEO

Nvidia is investing $3.5 billion into Taiwanese chipmaker MediaTek. As part of the deal, MediaTek will adopt Nvidia’s technology that will help it design custom chips for AI companies and hyperscalers that can be plugged directly into Nvidia-based data centers.
The deal comes as a growing number of AI companies and major cloud providers like Amazon, Google, Microsoft, OpenAI and Anthropic invest in building their own chips so they can be less reliant on Nvidia’s GPUs. Deals like this one with MediaTek allow Nvidia to cede ground to custom silicon while still maintaining its lead as the dominant data center scaffolding.
“Nvidia is an AI infrastructure company,” Dion Harris, Nvidia’s senior director of HPC and AI hyperscaler infrastructure solutions, said on Monday on a call with reporters. “We expanded beyond pure computing chips years ago.”
The partnership underscores the circular nature of Nvidia’s financing efforts over the past few years, which have often seen the chip giant investing in companies that flow back into its own ecosystem. The deal will give MediaTek access to Nvidia’s NVLink Fusion ecosystem, including NVLink, the technology that lets any chips — even if they’re not Nvidia’s chips — communicate with each other quickly.
Last week, Nvidia announced a similar partnership with Amazon Web Services, albeit without the direct investment. AWS will deploy an additional 2 million Nvidia GPUs across its infrastructure, and also integrate NVLink Fusion.
With the Nvidia partnership, MediaTek can continue to build custom chips designed by cloud companies or AI labs tailored to their workloads, leveraging Nvidia’s “proven scale-up and scale-out technology stack and ecosystem” and “rack-scale architecture.”
“Basically, every cloud, every model builder is deploying our platform in some shape, form, or fashion,” Harris said. “So by MediaTek being able to offer this extension to its customers, it allows them to standardize on the rack-scale infrastructure across their AI factories… and also deploy their [custom chips] right alongside those using the same standard platform.”
“This is really about opening up this ecosystem to the entire MediaTek customer base,” Harris continued.
MediaTek hasn’t publicly shared information about its customer base as it relates to custom AI chips, but it’s clear Nvidia aims to help it boost that side of the business so long as it can come along for the ride. MediaTek has been slowly building its custom data center ASIC (application-specific integrated circuit) operations, saying in June that it expects the business to generate $2 billion in revenue in 2026, and hopes to target more of the market in the coming years.
Given MediaTek’s expertise in developing custom chips that power smartphones , smart homes, automobiles, and wireless communications, the company will also continue to collaborate with Nvidia on DGX Spark, the company’s small developer-focused desktop AI computer. The companies have extended their collaboration with the RTX Spark, Nvidia’s push to put its AI tech into consumer AI PCs.
MediaTek and Nvidia will also continue “developing platforms for AI-powered, software-defined vehicles in the era of physical AI,” per a press release. MediaTek’s auto platforms rely on Nvidia’s RTX graphics for intelligent vehicle cockpits and work alongside Nvidia Drive AGX, the company’s in-car computing platform for autonomous driving workloads.
“AI is transforming every computing platform — from the world’s largest AI factories to the PC and the car,” Jensen Huang, founder and CEO of Nvidia, said in a statement. “Together, we’re building platforms that bring NVIDIA accelerated computing to new markets and give customers the freedom to create differentiated AI systems at enormous scale.”
